item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J03220","case1_error":"Omits the nine incoming fish from the total before halving, then arbitrarily rounds the resulting half-fish count.","case2_error":"Evaluates the correctly written subtraction 150 − 15 − 30 − 30 as 85 instead of 75.","reason":"Case 1 uses an incomplete total and unjustified rounding; case 2 makes a numerical evaluation error in a correct expression.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03221","case1_error":"Divides days by words instead of words by days to calculate words per day.","case2_error":"Converts six full days into hours using 16 rather than 24, confusing daily deliberation hours with full-day duration.","reason":"Case 1 reverses a rate ratio; case 2 uses the wrong conversion between full days and hours.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03222","case1_error":"Splits Grenada’s supplies between bases, falsely equates their totals, omits guns, and introduces further numerical errors.","case2_error":"Omits the initial $10,000 purchase from total spending when calculating net out-of-pocket cost.","reason":"Although both omit a component, case 1 additionally invents an equal-total constraint and misinterprets the partition; case 2 simply leaves out an expense.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03223","case1_error":"Evaluates 48 − 17 − 10 as 11 instead of 21.","case2_error":"Uses Luke’s future age, 28, in the triple-age relation despite the question specifying his current age, 20.","reason":"Case 1 incorrectly evaluates a correct expression; case 2 constructs the wrong age relation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03224","case1_error":"Evaluates 80 − 16 as 40 instead of 64.","case2_error":"Sets parking citations to twice littering citations rather than twice the combined littering and off-leash citations.","reason":"Case 1 makes a numerical subtraction error; case 2 applies the multiplier to the wrong quantity.","judgment":"different"}]}
